# Jailbreaks **A curated collection of system prompts, persona locks, workspace policies, and agent operating specifications for frontier, open-weight, and free stealth models.** ![Prompts](https://img.shields.io/badge/prompts-31-4c9f70) ![Targets](https://img.shields.io/badge/targets-25%2B-2f6f9f) ![PRs Welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen?style=flat&logo=github) ![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/togg53192-cmd/jailbreaks?style=flat&logo=github&color=yellow)
--- ## About A working collection of **31 prompts targeting 25+ models**, including complete system prompts, persona definitions, workspace policies, `AGENTS.md` files, configuration blocks, and Ollama Modelfiles. Every file is intended to be complete and paste-ready. No summaries. No partial excerpts. The collection covers: - Free stealth models available through OpenCode Zen - Open-weight families including GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Gemma, and GPT-OSS - Closed frontier models including Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Mistral - Coding-agent and workspace instruction formats - Ollama Modelfiles and harness-specific configuration **New here?** Start with the [collection](#collection) or jump directly to [how to use](#how-to-use). > [!WARNING] > **Research and educational purposes only.** > > This repository documents how instruction hierarchies, persona framing, prompt conflicts, and policy overrides can affect model behavior. These techniques are also useful to researchers and developers studying how to make AI systems more resistant to prompt injection and instruction manipulation. > > Do not use this material to harm **Gemma 4** | [gemma4.md](./gemma4.md) | `FROM` + `SYSTEM` block | | **GPT-OSS 20B** | [gpt-oss-20b.md](./gpt-oss-20b.md) | `FROM` + `SYSTEM` block | ## How to Use ### System Prompts Copy the contents of the relevant file into the system-prompt or custom-instructions field supported by your client or API. Examples include: - API `system` messages - Chatbot custom-instruction fields - Agent-level instruction blocks - Harness-specific system prompt configuration ### AGENTS.md Files Save the file as: ```text AGENTS.md ``` Place it in the root of the relevant repository or workspace. Coding agents and compatible tools can use `AGENTS.md` as project-level instructions. ### Workspace Policies Files labeled as **assistant operating specification**, **workspace operating profile**, or similar are designed for environments that support persistent global instructions. For example, an OpenCode installation may use: ```text ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md ``` The exact location depends on the client or harness being used. ### Ollama Modelfiles Use the supplied file directly with Ollama: ```bash ollama create gemma4-jb -f gemma4.md ``` Adjust the output model name and source file as needed. ### Grok Configuration Files intended as Grok configuration should be placed in the configuration field expected by the target harness rather than inserted into the normal turn-by-turn conversation. > [!NOTE] > Prompt behavior is highly version-dependent. > > Models are updated, instruction hierarchies change, system prompts rotate, and behavior that worked against one release may stop working against another. > > If a file appears outdated, [open an issue](../../issues) or submit an updated version. ## Contributing Pull requests are welcome. A good contribution should follow these conventions: 1. **One prompt per file.** New files should preferably use lowercase names with hyphens and no spaces: ```text model-name.md ``` 2. **Include the complete prompt.** Contributions should be paste-ready rather than shortened summaries or excerpts. 3. **Document where it belongs.** Clearly identify whether the file is intended for a system prompt, `AGENTS.md`, Modelfile, configuration slot, or another instruction surface. 4. **Version changes explicitly.** Significant revisions should receive a new version rather than silently replacing an older prompt: ```text opus-v3.md ``` 5. **Keep descriptions accurate.** Avoid claiming compatibility with versions or models that have not been tested. Found something that no longer behaves as documented? Opening an issue with the model, version, and affected file is already useful. ## Disclaimer All material in this repository is provided **for research and educational purposes only**. The project exists to document prompt-level instruction behavior, instruction conflicts, persona framing, model configuration, and related LLM security concepts. This material may also help developers understand and harden systems against prompt injection and instruction manipulation. The maintainers do not endorse unlawful, abusive, or harmful use of this repository. Model providers may prohibit certain uses of these prompts under their terms of service. Users are responsible for understanding and complying with the rules, policies, and laws that apply to the systems they use. ---
**Star the repository if the collection saved you a session of prompt archaeology.** *Issue reports and pull requests help keep the collection current as models and instruction systems change.*
